concepts.def: How quickly reactants are used up or products are formed per unit time.
Higher concentration means more particles per volume, more collisions per second, faster rate.
Higher T gives particles more energy, more frequent successful collisions, faster rate.
Smaller pieces give more surface area exposed, more collisions, faster rate.
Substance that speeds up a reaction without being used up by providing a lower-activation-energy pathway.
Track gas volume, mass loss, or solution colour change over time.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Rates of Reaction & Equilibrium — a core area of GCSE Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Rates of Reaction & Equilibrium brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Rates of Reaction & Equilibrium.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
